verdict.rationale: Reflect documents OAuth 2 credentials, including PKCE support, and its OpenAPI spec defines two OAuth2 scopes (read:graph / write:graph). An agent can therefore get a read-only or read-write token, which is real but coarse least-privilege scoping. missing for 10: finer-grained scopes (per-graph or per-endpoint limits), documented token lifetime, expiry and revocation controls, agent-specific credential guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: For authentication, we support OAuth 2. You will need to create credentials here.
GET /users/me with OAuth2 scopes read:graph / write:graph
We do support OAuth's PKCE extension which means you can build a client to Reflect without shipping secret keys around.
